pseudos.text: The tax-software company announced a major workforce reduction, with the chief executive telling staff that roughly 17% of the workforce will be cut. About 3,000 full-time roles are being eliminated as part of a difficult corporate decision to co-locate teams and accelerate AI work. Offices in Reno and Woodland Hills are winding down, and affected employees were offered a severance package of 16 weeks' base pay plus additional compensation based on tenure.

Workers losing their jobs at a large corporation are facing sudden career disruption after the employer cutting thousands of jobs announced the closure of specific office locations. The company's chief executive delivered the bad news, framing the move as a strategic business rationale for the cuts. While a severance package is offered, many ordinary people are now dealing with the end of their local workplaces in Reno and Woodland Hills.

Ordinary people facing a sudden career disruption are bearing the cost of the company's strategic shift, with 3,000 people and their households directly impacted by the decision. The executive delivering the bad news announced a top-down mandate affecting thousands of workers, and while a financial cushion is offered to help workers transition, local economies in two cities are losing a corporate presence as offices wind down.
